stem: A client taking allopurinol develops a new skin rash. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue allopurinol and monitor the rash at home until the next routine visit.
options.B: Hold one dose and restart allopurinol once the rash fades without further evaluation.
options.C: Stop allopurinol immediately and seek prompt medical attention for possible hypersensitivity.
options.D: Increase the allopurinol dose because a rash suggests inadequate urate lowering.

rationale: The current allopurinol label directs immediate discontinuation when a skin rash develops and instructs patients to seek medical attention promptly because serious hypersensitivity reactions, including severe cutaneous reactions, can occur. Therefore C is correct. A continues a drug the label says to stop. B conflicts with the direction to discontinue permanently at the first rash or other sign of hypersensitivity. D has no basis in the label and would increase exposure to a suspected offending drug.
educational_objective: Teach clients taking allopurinol to stop the medication immediately and seek prompt medical attention if a new rash develops because it may signal serious hypersensitivity.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_version_date: Version 103; DailyMed updated 2026-04-13; prescribing information revised 2026-04
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.1 Skin Rash and Hypersensitivity; Patient instruction within §5.1 to stop immediately and seek medical attention promptly
source_claim_supported: Allopurinol is associated with serious and sometimes fatal dermatologic hypersensitivity reactions; the label directs permanent discontinuation at the first appearance of rash or other hypersensitivity signs and instructs patients to stop immediately and seek prompt medical attention if a rash develops.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: Educate client about medications; Evaluate client response to medication; Handle and administer high-risk medications safely
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — allopurinol hypersensitivity and patient teaching
correction_summary: Tightened the stem and rebuilt the alternatives around the exact current label instruction: stop allopurinol immediately and seek prompt medical attention for any new rash. Removed topical-treatment and diagnostic-padding distractors and reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
